text:
Dmitri: Quick heads-up — ran a replay of the long-context prefills against the canary runtime (kernels v3.8) and saw a consistent ~12% p99 increase compared to v3.6. Replay harness + seqdist attached, looking for suggestions on where to start.

Alice: Oof. Is that for the prefill-dominant traces only or also for mixed traffic?

Dmitri: Mostly prefill-heavy. Mixed traffic shows <3% change. The regression scales with prefill length: >3k tokens worse.

Ben: Can you paste the profiler flame or a short hotspot list?

Dmitri: Sure — snippet from perf-profile (onclick filtered to gpu kernels):
```
time (ms)  kernel_name                   %
120        attention_cuda_v2             45
85         matmul_large_tile             33
40         kv_cache_store                10
25         memory_copy_host_to_device    6
```
I expected attention_cuda_v2 to be dominant, not matmul.

Carla: That matmul bump smells like a kernelselect fallback. Did the planner pick a different kernel for long seqlen? Could be a tiling change triggered by quantization profile.

Eva: Also check batching info from the trace. If continuous-batcher is shrinking batches during prefill (because of headroom limits) you amplify kernel overheads. Do we have per-step batch size distribution?

Dmitri: Yep. From the loadtrace: most steps are batch=1 during prefill because the harness uses force-prefill-concurrency=1 to emulate heavy prefix behavior. Batch distribution: 70% batch=1 prefill steps, 25% batch=2, 5% batch>=4.

Ben: Ah — apples-to-apples: v3.6 used a different kernel selection heuristic that preferred large-tile matmul for batch>1, but for batch=1 it had a small-tile attention path. v3.8's heuristics may choose matmul_large_tile for seqlen>2048 even at batch=1 which would be slower.

Carla: Also check KV cache behavior — we recently changed prefill chunking to 512-token chunks. If the cache_store path does more memcopies per chunk you pay both memcpy + matmul alignment overhead. Any delta in kv hit ratio?

Dmitri: Good call. KV hit rate fell from 98.4% to 97.1% in the failing runs because the replay harness prefill chunk boundaries shifted. That increased store ops by ~18k per 100k requests.

Eva: Suggestion: for a tight root-cause, run two replays: (A) deterministic kernel selection forced to v3.6 heuristics (kernelselect flag), (B) disable adaptive chunking (prefill-chunk-size fixed to previous value). Keep all other settings identical. That isolates kernel vs KV chunking.

Dmitri: Running those now. Commands used: 
```bash
./replay_harness --trace long-prefill-2026 --kernelselect-mode legacy --concurrency 16 --force-batch=auto
./replay_harness --trace long-prefill-2026 --kv-chunk-size 1024 --concurrency 16 --force-batch=auto
```
Will share diffs when complete.

replay-bot: Replay started (id=r-2026-11). 100k requests expected. ETA ~6m. :rocket:

Alice: When you share diffs, include the microtraces: per-step kernel chosen, batch size, kv ops, memcpy counts. Makes the apples-to-apples comparison quicker.

Ben: If kernelselect is the culprit we should add a unit test in the kernelselect harness to check kernel rank ordering for seqlen bands (<=512,512-2048,>2048) and batch sizes (1,2,4). Failing that, revert the heuristic for >2048 until we tune.

Dmitri: Early results: legacy kernelselect run brings p99 back down ~9% vs v3.8 baseline (so most of regression is kernelselect). Fix confirmed by disabling kernel change.

Carla: Nice. That still leaves the KV hit regressions — they may explain the remaining gap. Any plan to stabilize chunking boundaries in the harness?

Dmitri: We'll pin kv-chunk-size to 1024 in the replay harness for the next apples-to-apples round. Also going to run a synthetic traffic test (uniform seqlen sampling) to see if the regression shows up there — helps rule out harness artifacts.

Eva: For the synthetic test, make sure to seed RNG and use identical batching config (disable adaptive batching) so it's deterministic. Also capture GPU kernel launch counts; that made the difference visible for us previously.

Dmitri: Agreed. Next steps: 1) create short PR to revert kernelselect heuristic for >2048 until we tune; 2) run pinned-kv-chunk replay + synthetic seeded run; 3) add kernelselect unit tests for the seqlen/batch matrix. I'll open tickets and tag owners.

Ben: Ping me on the PR review for the kernelselect revert. I can help write the test matrix.

Alice: Thanks team. This thread is a good template for perf triage — kernel vs KV vs batch.

Dmitri: Posting final numbers when both replays finish. Thanks. :thumbsup:
